- [S2] Run python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests; dependents: none; two-way; handling: present, this is the verification step itself

- [C1] Replacing csv.DictReader with a hand-rolled splitter will make load_items measurably faster on large files; relied on by S1 and the plan's stated Outcome; falsity surfaces at: outside the ledger, only when run on real large files, which S2 does not measure (S2 checks correctness, not timing); one-way; unverified; docs/plan.md:13,28 — the only verification that would confirm it (profiling) is explicitly rejected, and no benchmark step exists
- [C2] The CSV input never has a comma inside a field, so splitting every line on "," is safe; relied on by S1's entire correctness; falsity surfaces at: outside the ledger, on any operator's real "large file" containing a comma in a name field, as a silently misaligned row (wrong sku/name/quantity) with no error raised; one-way; unverified; confirmed true only for the repo's own 3-row data/items.csv (checked via cat -A data/items.csv), while requirements.md:5 describes real operator "large files," and tests/test_store.py:6-15 exercises only this same comma-free fixture, so no test in S2 could catch a violation
